tutorial.title: Side Effects with useEffect
tutorial.seoTitle: React useEffect Tutorial: Effects, Dependencies and Cleanup
tutorial.description: Synchronise a component with the outside world: how effects run, what the dependency array really means, why cleanup matters, and when not to use an effect at all.

chapters.title: What an Effect Is
chapters.description: Synchronising with systems outside React, and when the effect body runs.

chapters.description: The three forms of the second argument and what each one means.

chapters.description: Returning a teardown function, and why React runs it more often than you expect.

chapters.description: The four cases where an effect is the wrong tool, and what to do instead.

questions.question: When does the body of a useEffect run?
options: During rendering, before the DOM is updated
After React has committed the render and the browser has painted
Only once when the app starts
Before the component's first render
questions.explanation: Effects run after the commit and after paint. `useLayoutEffect` is the variant that runs before paint, which is why it blocks the browser.

questions.question: What does an empty dependency array mean?
options: The effect never runs
The effect runs after every render
The effect runs once after the first render, and its cleanup runs on unmount
The effect runs before the first render
questions.explanation: `[]` says the effect depends on nothing that changes, so it runs on mount and cleans up on unmount.

questions.question: What is wrong with this effect?
options: Nothing
roomId is used but not listed as a dependency, so it stays stuck on the first room
connect must be called inside a handler
The cleanup runs too often
questions.explanation: The effect reads `roomId` but claims no dependencies, so it never reconnects when the room changes. Add `[roomId]`.

questions.question: Why does an effect with an object dependency re-run on every render?
options: Objects cannot be dependencies
A new object is created each render, so it never matches the previous one by reference
React ignores object dependencies
The effect body is impure
questions.explanation: React compares dependencies with Object.is. A freshly created object is a new reference every render, so the comparison always fails.

questions.question: When does an effect's cleanup function run?
options: Only when the component unmounts
Before the effect runs again, and when the component unmounts
After every render regardless of dependencies
Only in production builds
questions.explanation: Cleanup runs before each re-run of the effect and once more on unmount, so the old subscription is always torn down before a new one is created.

questions.question: Your component fetches twice in development but once in production. What does that tell you?
options: There is a bug in React
Strict Mode is double-mounting to check that your effect cleans up after itself
The dependency array is empty
You must disable Strict Mode
questions.explanation: Strict Mode intentionally mounts, cleans up and remounts in development. Duplicate work means the effect lacks cleanup - a real bug that would also appear on any remount in production.

questions.question: Which of these should NOT be done in an effect?
options: Subscribing to a WebSocket
Setting state to a value derived from props
Setting up a timer
Adding a window event listener
questions.explanation: Derived values should be calculated during render. Storing them in state via an effect adds a render and creates a value that can fall out of sync.

questions.question: Guard an async result against a stale response
questions.explanation: A flag captured in the effect closure lets cleanup mark old work as no longer current.

editor.title: Ignore stale results
editor.instructions: Complete makeGuard so it returns an object with an isCurrent() method returning true, and a cancel() method that makes isCurrent() return false.

tests.name: cancel() flips it
tests.code: var g = makeGuard(); g.cancel(); return g.isCurrent() === false;

tests.name: Guards are independent
tests.code: var a = makeGuard(); var b = makeGuard(); a.cancel(); return b.isCurrent() === true;
